turnaround_reason: Forward Air is down ~70% since its debt-funded Omni Logistics merger left it with ~$1.68B net debt at ~5.5x EBITDA — right at its covenant limit. A Goldman-advised strategic review raised hopes of a full-company sale, but a full sale is now seen as unlikely, sending shares lower. It is basing near lows on a fading M&A catalyst.
bullish_points: Strategic review is nearing conclusion; even a partial outcome (Omni unit divestitures) could de-lever and reduce the covenant risk
~$2.5B trailing revenue on a ~$545M market cap — enormous operating leverage to any margin recovery or successful sale
Piecemeal Omni divestitures have begun (one unit closed July 2026), showing the board is executing on de-leveraging
If freight cycle recovers, EBITDA growth alone could pull the leverage ratio back below the covenant
bearish_points: A full-company sale is now viewed as unlikely — the primary near-term catalyst just deflated, and the stock fell ~9% in 5 days on it
Net debt ~5.5x EBITDA sits exactly at the covenant limit; any EBITDA slippage risks a breach and equity impairment
Q2 posted a loss on a $244M impairment — the underlying business is still deteriorating
Divestitures so far are tiny (~$16.5M) relative to a ~$1.7B debt problem — nowhere near a fix
This is a broken-balance-sheet equity: the payoff is binary and skewed to the downside if the review disappoints
catalyst: Conclusion of the strategic review — a larger Omni divestiture or refinancing that materially cuts leverage below the covenant limit
catalyst_timing: Next 1-2 quarters as the review concludes
suggested_trade: Pass / watch-only; if taken, a very small speculative spot near $16 sized as an option-like bet on the review outcome
key_risk: The strategic review ends with no transformative deal while EBITDA slips, breaching covenants and severely impairing the equity
would_skip_if: You are not comfortable with covenant-breach / equity-wipe risk — the fading full-sale catalyst removed the main reason to own it here
